newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian nuclear plant reports minor incident.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian nuclear plant reports minor incident.

text.p: Bulgaria's nuclear power plant at Kozloduy reported on Tuesday a minor technical failure in a steam generator of its newest unit.

No radioactive material was invovled in the incident which affected the 1,000-megawatt reactor number six, the plant's acting chairman Kiril Nikolov said, adding that afterwards the the reactor had been unplugged from the national energy grid.

Reached by telephone in Kozloduy, he said experts at this stage assessed the incident as zero according to the International Nuclear Event Scale (INES) and the failure was too minor to cause any danger.
"Our first assessment shows that most probably the fault has been caused by a leak of a small tube in the reactor's second steam generator," Nikolov told Reuters.

Bulgaria, which lacks energy resources, relies on all six Kozloduy reactors to avoid a power crisis this winter. The 3,760-megawatt plant on the Danube river provides almost half of the country's power needs.
Kozloduy switched off its oldest 440-megawatt reactor in May amid international concern over the safety of its vessel's metal.

Energy officials said the first results of analysis of the metal's samples carried out by Russia's Korchatov Institute showed the metal was in good condition and could be put in operation this winter.
